name: quest
title: Quest
description: A named task with a reward on it and a way of reading how far through it the player is. A quest is measured one of two ways, and both are this component rather than two: pass `steps` for a task counted in discrete things done, which renders the shared `segments`, and pass `value` with `max` for one counted in a continuous number, which renders `progress-bar`. Never both, so one number is never shown two ways at once. There is no `data-gs-progress` and no `data-gs-fill`: how far through it is, is `data-gs-value` over `data-gs-max`, and the nested component carries the same pair because it is the same number. The reward pill rides on `data-gs-reward`, the same attribute a reward object uses. Complete shows a tick and locked shows a padlock, so neither state is a colour alone. Performs nothing: it never counts what the player did, awards the reward, or decides the quest is finished.
docs: Pass `title` for what the quest asks, `detail` for the line under it, and `reward` for the pill, with `rewardId` when the host has its own id for it. Then pass either `steps`, one entry per discrete thing the quest asks for, or `value` with `max`. Pass `complete` when the host says the quest is finished; the component never infers it from every step being done, because a reward the host has not settled must not look settled. Pass `locked` for a quest that opens later, which keeps its shape and shows a padlock. It imports `./progress-bar` and `./segments`, which are the flat paths a `gamestage-ui add` produces, and `@gamestage/progress-bar` and `@gamestage/segments` are what put those files there.
